name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,336

clue.text: Act enthusiastically when Dorothy's companion turns up in a dress

indicators.note: in a down entry, something turning up is read from the bottom upwards, so the companion's name runs backwards
being in a garment means sitting inside it, so the dress wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a gown is a long dress
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited when a little dog appears wearing a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy is the heroine of The Wizard of Oz, and her companion is her dog; the dress is wrapped around his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to town is an idiom for doing something with great energy and lavishness.

clue.text: Trustworthy leaders of society are found taking ecstasy

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Respectable society figures are caught using drugs, which hardly makes them trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something safe is reliable and can be depended on, a close synonym of trustworthy.

clue.text: Struck by a story put up by female newspaper boss

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie, a story
F is the standard abbreviation for female
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone is hit by a tale planted by a woman who edits a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' here means a lie, not a news item, despite the newspaper setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To biff is informal for to hit someone, so biffed is a slangy synonym for struck.

clue.text: Soldiers having to deal with retirement

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to treat a matter is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Troops are left to cope with withdrawing from the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface makes retirement look like an army pulling back, which is exactly the sense used.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal, and retirement in its old sense means withdrawing to a quiet place.

clue.text: Foolishly agree with Lot's confidant

indicators.note: acting foolishly means acting without order or sense, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical aside: someone rashly sides with Lot's trusted adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot looks like the biblical figure owning the confidant, but the name is just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is an intimate friend one trusts completely.

clue.text: Single girl longed to possess Otto's heart

indicators.note: a heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the name are kept
to possess something is to hold it, so the outer pieces enclose what follows

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
the two central letters of this name
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman pined to win the affections of a man called Otto.
explanation.walkthrough: UNA and ACHED together hold the TT from the middle of OTTO, giving UNATTACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattached describes someone not in a relationship, the same as being single.

clue.text: Fellow after information on international friendly

indicators.note: coming after means placed later in the word, so the fellow goes at the end

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
I is an abbreviation for international
Al is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A man follows the data on a friendly international football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International friendly' reads as a sports fixture; in fact the two words are split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means warm and cheerful in manner, a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Detestable to describe books covering the return of Capone as explosive

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the gangster's name is read backwards
a cover wraps around something, so the books enclose the reversed name
to describe in the geometric sense is to draw a line around, so the detestable word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: vile means hateful or detestable
OT is the Old Testament, the standard crossword books
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Books about Al Capone's comeback described as hateful and incendiary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing around, not telling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile means liable to blow up suddenly, so it is a near synonym of explosive.

clue.text: Initially naive to supply Spike with a weapon

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
supplying the drink with something puts it inside, so the letter goes into the word

blocks.note: to spike a drink is to lace it
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A naive person arms someone called Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike looks like a name or a sharp point, but it is the verb meaning to add alcohol or a drug to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Tolerated back in Esher obviously

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters across the following words
going back means reading from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Something was clearly put up with in Esher, a well-off Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London; here it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, and to bear something is to tolerate it.

clue.text: Definitely in favour of creating changes without a hint of glitz

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of the following word is meant
without means lacking, so that letter is removed
changes signals that the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: being for something means supporting it
taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is firmly in support of making alterations that drop the showbiz sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is a set phrase meaning surely, without doubt, the same as definitely.

clue.text: Oddly cool about sketch of chicken

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on
turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the first and third letters of this word
to sketch is to draw

explanation.surface: A strangely relaxed attitude to a drawing of a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken is the slang sense of a cowardly person, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is informal for a timid person who lacks courage, a coward.

clue.text: Right to stop allowance after Lincoln's moral lapse

indicators.note: stopping a hole means plugging it, so the letter is put inside the word
placed after means this part comes later in the answer

blocks.note: Abe is the nickname of US President Abraham Lincoln
a ration is a fixed allowance
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sense of what is right curbing a stipend becomes Lincoln's ethical slip.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes just inside RATION, after its own R, so the doubled R appears in the middle of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from normal or proper conduct, so a moral lapse is one kind.

clue.text: Easily persuaded soldiers to invade key island from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading from right to left
invaders move inside a territory, so the soldiers go within the other letters

blocks.note: A is a musical key
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops are readily talked into storming a crucial island from its eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key island' reads as a strategic target, but key is the musical A and the island is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means responsive and willing to agree, so it fits someone easily persuaded.

clue.text: Extremely serious when concerned with the future for example

blocks.note: being in a field means being involved or concerned with it
the future is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Talk about the future gets very grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The future is meant grammatically, as one of the verb tenses, not as the time to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means of extreme degree or earnestness, so it suits something extremely serious.

clue.text: A good way to obstruct someone looking for salt

indicators.note: obstructing means getting in the way, so the phrase sits in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: a good way off is far away, afar
a seer is one who sees

explanation.surface: A useful method for blocking someone who wants table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking for salt' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is only a link and salt is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran sailor, so salt alone means a seafarer.

clue.text: An expression of finality in that respect follows accordingly

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first phrase goes at the end

blocks.note: so means therefore, accordingly
there can mean in that matter or respect

explanation.surface: A pedantic phrase-book note: a final word comes after a logical conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: So there is a defiant exclamation used to end an argument, closing the matter.

clue.text: Freed from anxiety about the first woman to break cover

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the woman goes within the cover

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a lid is a cover
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A tale of being relieved of worry about the original woman bursting out of hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved describes the feeling when worry lifts, so it means freed from anxiety.

clue.text: Revolutionary's endless poetry of defeat

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A rebel's never-ending poems about losing a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a military setback or a loss, a synonym of defeat.

clue.text: Gamble on Five's opening song becoming a legitimate target for ridicule

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the number is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
an air is a tune or song
a game is a risky bet, as in being game for a gamble

explanation.surface: Betting on a Channel 5 opening number that gets mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the gamble goes at the end; Five is also a British TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game is an idiom for someone who may rightly be mocked or criticised.

clue.text: Turn on American runner after start of race

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is used

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for American
the opening letter of this word
a runner is a river; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A US athlete warms up once the race has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is the crossword river, not an athlete; the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone on is to excite them, which is what arousing means.

clue.text: Falsify dossier to frame religious scholar

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so the file encloses the scholar

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of papers
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: Doctoring documents to set up an innocent theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' sounds like stitching someone up, which fits the crime story, but it means to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle accounts or figures is informal for falsifying them dishonestly.

clue.text: Unconvincing complaint raised by the French

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A weak grievance lodged by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble excuse or argument is weak and fails to persuade, so it is unconvincing.

clue.text: Dispute with flyer featured in short story

indicators.note: being featured in a story means appearing inside it, so the bird sits within

blocks.note: a conte is a short story, from the French
a raven is a bird, a flyer

explanation.surface: An argument about a pilot appearing in a brief tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Flyer suggests an aviator or a leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a claim is to deny or challenge it, so it can mean to dispute.

clue.text: Appear half-hearted about tenor's arrest

indicators.note: losing half its heart means one of the two central letters goes
about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the musical voice

blocks.note: to seem is to appear
T is an abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A singer looks unenthusiastic about being taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' means to halt, not to detain a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it, which is the sense of arrest as halting.

clue.text: Told to go before leaving a gift

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that piece is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed before leaving behind a farewell gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent away means being ordered to depart, so sent works for told to go.

clue.text: Painful to accept Conservative account

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so the abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: sore means painful
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: It hurts to take on board the Tory version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a score is to settle an account, a reckoning of what is owed.

clue.text: Sincere about limiting length of exhaust attachment

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are jumbled
limiting something means enclosing it within bounds, so the jumbled word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A genuine take on keeping the length of a car's tailpipe fitting in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer is a muffler fitted to an engine's exhaust to reduce its noise.
